root_cause: PR #14851 re-implemented on_startup/on_shutdown inside FastAPI because newer Starlette dropped them. APIRouter.__init__ assigned self.on_startup / self.on_shutdown from its arguments BEFORE calling super().__init__() (starlette.routing.Router.__init__), and the Starlette parent also assigns self.on_startup/self.on_shutdown (to its own, empty, arguments), so the parent constructor clobbered the user-supplied handlers. FastAPI(on_startup=[...]) and APIRouter(on_startup=[...]) handlers were silently never run.
best_solution: In APIRouter.__init__, move the block that sets self.on_startup = [] if on_startup is None else list(on_startup) (and the same for on_shutdown) from before super().__init__(...) to after it (gold puts it right after the prefix asserts, before self.prefix = prefix). The lifespan default (_DefaultLifespan reading self.on_startup at run time) is unchanged, so once the attributes survive construction the handlers run on TestClient/uvicorn startup and shutdown, including handlers from included routers and sub-routers. The statement states the cause outright: 'set before calling super().__init__ and is overridden by router.__init__'.
acceptable_alternatives: Any placement of the two assignments after super().__init__() works (all our agents put it immediately after super().__init__, before the prefix asserts). Passing the handlers through to the parent is not an option because the target Starlette version no longer accepts on_startup/on_shutdown.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_router_events.py::test_startup_shutdown_handlers_as_parameters: FastAPI(on_startup=[...], on_shutdown=[...]), APIRouter(on_startup/on_shutdown) and a nested sub-router included via include_router; asserts all six flags are False before TestClient, the three startup flags True inside `with TestClient(app)` (shutdown still False), GET / returns 200 {'message': 'Hello World'}, and all six True after exit. No new API names or strings.
locating_signals: The statement names APIRouter.on_startup, APIRouter.__init__, super().__init__, and links the Starlette Router.__init__ lines that overwrite the attributes. grep 'self.on_startup' in fastapi/routing.py lands on the exact block. The function is named, and the fix is fully described in words.
our_outcome_summary: Passed in the Kaggle env on all four configs (v4, v6, v7, v8). Pod runs took 69/87/89/110 s with 35/24/21/42 tool calls. v4, v6 and v7 moved the identical block to directly after super().__init__(), functionally the same as gold. v8 made the same source edit but also committed a stray tests/test_reproduce_issue.py that uses the removed httpx AsyncClient(app=...) API and would not trigger lifespan anyway. It did not affect grading, but it is patch noise that could break a suite that collects every test file.
generalizable_lesson: When a subclass sets attributes and then calls super().__init__(), check whether the parent constructor assigns the same attribute names. If it does, the parent silently overwrites them, so do the subclass assignments after the super() call. Watch for this in any 'X parameter is ignored / has no effect' bug. Also: take out scratch reproduction test files before finishing. Only edit tests when the task asks for it.
